key_insight: Optimizing each weight matrix independently is not enough for LLM compression; a three-level pipeline that expands from matrix-wise SVD to block-wise joint optimization and then end-to-end refinement achieves much lower perplexity.
engineering_relevance: For practical model compression, the method shows that block-level coupling can be as important as per-layer optimality, guiding how to trade calibration data, compute, and quality in deployment pipelines.
method: L1: whitened SVD truncation on individual matrices using 256 calibration sequences.
L2: joint optimization over each Transformer block to correct compounded nonlinear errors.
L3: end-to-end language-model loss refinement for final perplexity improvement.
evidence_signal: On LLaMA-7B at 60% compression, WikiText-2 perplexity improved from 42.1 to 19.1 to 11.4 across the three levels, with gains reported across 20-80% compression and multiple architectures.
watch_item: Results emphasize perplexity and compression fidelity rather than downstream task accuracy, and the cross-architecture comparisons used architecture-specific settings rather than one uniform protocol.
paper_title: Per-Matrix Optimality Is Not Enough: Three-Level Optimization for Low-Rank LLM Compression
